title: [Performance][MRV2] Share per-step PCP metadata across KV-cache groups
body: ### What this PR does / why we need it? This PR reduces attention metadata construction overhead for DeepSeek V4 with model runner v2 and PCP, and extends compatible optimizations to DSpark DSA SWA drafting. Previously, cache-group builders independently prepared metadata even when much of the work was identical across groups. The global PCP path also built query-related metadata although its consumers only needed to update caches. Profiling identified this repeated preparation as a significant contributor to build_attn_metadata() latency. The implementation introduces a shared metadata plan with three main optimizations: 1. Build metadata according to consumer requirements. - Distinguish compressor state-cache, SWA, attention, and indexer consumers. - Build lightweight metadata for state-cache consumers. - Prepare SAS metadata only for attention consumers and QLI metadata only for indexer consumers. - Restrict global PCP metadata to fields required for cache updates, avoiding unnecessary query metadata construction. 2. Reuse batch-level PCP preparation across cache groups. - Prepare graph-compatible restore indices and padded query offsets once per execution. - Share request-level calculations and RoPE preparation. - Stage global RoPE into persistent buffers once for sharded decode with full graphs. 3. Share stable SAS/QLI outputs across compatible groups. - Reuse the prepared metadata buffers directly, avoiding repeated copies into individual builders. - Share QLI sequence-length and residual calculations. - Keep computed results scoped to each execution while retaining persistent output buffers for stable addresses. The PR also integrates the supported DSpark DSA SWA draft path. It preserves the non-causal SWA window and group-specific physical indices, separates ordinary and DSpark SAS variants, and uses independent target/draft plans and RoPE buffers. Mixed target/MTP SWA groups remain eligible for target optimization rather than being excluded solely because they contain draft layer names. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? No API or configuration changes. This PR reduces attention metadata preparation overhead for DeepSeek V4 PCP and supported DSpark paths, with no intended change to model outputs. ### How was this patch tested? This optimization was benchmarked and accuracy-tested on DeepSeekV4-Flash-w4a8 across 8× 910B NPUs with TP=4 and PCP=2. ### Results Before the optimization, build_attn_metadata() took an average of 21.2 ms. At 4 concurrent requests with an input token count of 50k and output token count of 350, the average output token throughput was 75 tok/s. The profile before the modification: After the optimization, build_attn_metadata() takes an average of 9.8 ms, a performance improvement of about 53.8%. At 4 concurrent requests with an input token count of 50k and an output token count of 350, the average output token throughput is 83.8 tok/s, an improvement of about 11.7%.
